Subject: Stately onboarding blockers — signer evidence + PO ACK SLA

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick responses so far. Two items are blocking our procurement intake for Redwood in Coupa:

1) Signer evidence / signatory matrix: our security and procurement teams need documented proof of authorized signers (signed W9 + insurance cert already requested) but they asked whether Redwood can provide a notarized proof-of-authority or a KBA/ID verification report for the account owner. They flagged that the signature block on the redlined MSA isn't sufficient for our audit.

2) PO acknowledgement SLA mismatch: our Coupa integration expects an ACK within 48 hours and we've been told Redwood's standard is 72 hours for some vendor profiles. That mismatch will cause automatic hold rules in our PO workflow.

I've attached our local redlines and the vendor intake checklist for reference. Can you confirm what evidence you can provide and whether Redwood can map the ACK window on a per-account basis?

Appreciate a short timeline so we can keep our supplier activation sprint on schedule.

Best,

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed both Redwood_MSA_redline_v1.pdf and Stately_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf. High-level legal notes:

1) Signatory evidence: Redwood can provide notarized proof-of-authority as a one-time deliverable — Legal will need the full name, title, and government ID for the signer we notarize, plus a corporate resolution template executed by the customer (Stately) if they request cross-authorization. If Stately insists on continuous identity verification (KBA), we need to scope a recurring verification SOW.

2) MSA redlines: I marked three redlines that we will not accept without escalation: indemnity carve-outs that exceed our standard liability cap, unilateral audit rights, and a change to our data retention clause (we should offer a compromise — 180 days log retention + SOC2 SOC report access).

3) PO ACK SLA: we can accept a conditional clause that binds us to a 48-hour ACK "for electronically submitted POs with valid headers and item mapping". Legal suggests explicit language for exceptions (e.g., data errors, mapping failures, force majeure) and a cure period. That keeps the commercial ask intact while protecting us operationally.

Timeline: Legal can produce a clean MSA with comments incorporated within 3 business days after we receive the final Stately redlines + signer details. If Stately needs notarization, plan for 5–7 business days for scheduling and documentation.

I've attached a short legal comments doc for the account.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
